name: ceyx-heif-stack
description: Consuming manifest for the product build's vcpkg-supplied third-party stack: the HEIF stack (libheif + libde265 + kvazaar + aom) plus libwebp. Round-2 began this as the OD-2 overlay-port spike; D5 makes it load-bearing for the product build.
$comment-dependencies: libde265 and aom already arrive as transitive dependencies of libheif; they are ALSO listed explicitly because D5 consumes them directly (libde265 via the LIBDE265_* pre-seeding, aom via AOM_*), and a direct consumer must be a direct dependency -- otherwise a future libheif feature change could silently drop them from the install plan. libwebp has no path to this graph other than being declared here.
$comment-overrides: N30: nothing floats with the baseline. libwebp and aom are REGISTRY ports, so an explicit override is what pins them. libde265 is deliberately absent from this list: it is supplied by the overlay port native/vcpkg/ports/libde265 (a fork), and overlay ports bypass the versions database entirely -- a version constraint cannot be applied to them. Its 1.1.1 pin is the literal `version` field in that port's own vcpkg.json, which is a stronger pin than an override (it selects the exact source tarball by SHA-512 in portfile.cmake).
